subject: geography
title: UK Physical Landscapes Adventure: Foundations
welcome_lead: From the rocky Highlands to flat East Anglia — Britain's landscape is shaped by rock and ice.
meta_desc: GCSE Geography UK physical landscapes — uplands, lowlands, rock types, drainage.
final_note: You can now describe the basic UK relief and identify the three rock types.

concepts.def: High ground — mountains and hills (mostly NW UK)
Low flat ground — under 200m (mostly SE UK)
Land area drained by a river and its tributaries

walkthroughs.body_html:
Imagine a line from the mouth of the Tees (NE) to the mouth of the Exe (SW). North-west of it: uplands. South-east: lowlands.

Uplands: Scottish Highlands, Lake District, Snowdonia, Pennines. Made of old, hard igneous and metamorphic rock.

Lowlands: East Anglia, the South-East, the Midlands. Younger, softer sedimentary rocks.

Igneous (e.g. granite of Dartmoor): cooled magma — hard, resistant.

Sedimentary (e.g. chalk of South Downs, limestone of Cotswolds): layered, often softer.

Metamorphic (e.g. slate of Snowdonia): squashed/heated rock — very hard.

A drainage basin is the land drained by a river.

The watershed is the boundary between two basins. The source is where the river starts; the mouth is where it meets the sea.

UK's longest river is the Severn (~354 km).
